title: experience in rust vs godot game dev
author: sfscsdsf
selftext: is it much more difficult to build proper games through rust than godot?

comments.author: CoolestSlave
comments.body: I'm not a gamedev, but i think it will create you problem in the future if you don't use a proper game engine.

comments.author: Schaf-Unschaf
comments.body:
Not comparable. Rust is the language, like GDScript.
If you compare it with Bevy (including Avian/Parry and Lightyear), then it is more difficult as you are lacking the UI for doing stuff.

But Bevy is still great and continues getting developed and improved. The 0.19 and 0.20 versions were great updates, feature and performance wise.

Personally, I like the "no UI" approach of Bevy more.

comments.author: Relevant-Positive-48
comments.body:
Your question really isn't rust vs godot - it's using a game engine vs letting the AI build a custom one.  

For right now I'm a huge proponent of using a game engine.  It just makes easier.  A few examples:  
  
1.  Using commonly known tools works better if, say, your game gets really successful, and you want to bring on team members.

2.  You don't have to burn a ton of tokens building for multiple platforms as most of it is already there.

3.  Other AI tools you might use (3D model generators, music generators, video generators) are building pipelines to the major engines.

It'll get to a point where it won't matter (Like you'll be able to seamlessly do cross platform builds, port from a custom to an established engine really fast, or just have a team member can just hand you an asset that AI can effortlessly integrate) but I think we're still a little bit of time away from that.
